speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have been experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to help me determine the cause, please describe exactly when these symptoms started and how severe the pain is on a scale of 1 to 10. REQUEST TEST: Basic_Metabolic_Panel.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you; the basic metabolic panel results are normal. Given your persistent vomiting and chest pain, please describe the specific location and character of the pain, and whether it radiates to your arm, jaw, or back. REQUEST TEST: Cardiac_Enzymes.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you; the cardiac enzyme results are also normal, which helps rule out a heart attack. Since your pain persists despite normal metabolic and cardiac workups, can you describe the exact nature of the pain (e.g., burning, pressure) and whether it worsens when you lean forward or take a deep breath?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture).

The combination of forceful vomiting after heavy alcohol consumption, followed by severe chest pain and difficulty breathing, is classic for this condition. Given the risk of mediastinitis, I need to confirm this immediately.

REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CTA_with_contrast.
